subsystems.name: Imaging
subsystems.role: resolve every neuron, axon and synapse in a preserved human brain at nanometre resolution.
parts: automated sectioning or serial block-face systems

subsystems.name: Reconstruction pipeline
subsystems.role: turn petabytes of images into a wiring diagram.

subsystems.name: Parameter extraction
subsystems.role: infer not just who connects to whom, but how strongly and with what dynamics.

subsystems.name: Emulation model
parts: neuron model (from simple point neurons to detailed multi-compartment models)

subsystems.name: Compute substrate
subsystems.role: run the model fast enough to keep up with real time.

subsystems.name: Interface and persistence
subsystems.role: give the emulation senses, actions and a stable place to run.

subsystems.name: Validation
subsystems.role: test whether the copy behaves like, or is, the original person.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the brain
buildSteps.detail: For a theoretical whole-brain emulation the tissue would first be chemically fixed, or ideally cryo-preserved and then fixed, so the wiring stops changing. No method today preserves a whole human brain well enough to trace every synapse.

buildSteps.title: Section and image
buildSteps.detail: The brain would be cut into tens of thousands of thin slices and each imaged by electron microscopy, or imaged block-face layer by layer — roughly a petabyte-scale dataset per cubic millimetre.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the wiring
buildSteps.detail: Automated software aligns the images, segments neurons and traces axons and dendrites; human proofreaders correct errors. A full adult fruit-fly brain took this route and was published in 2024; a human brain is roughly six orders of magnitude larger.

buildSteps.title: Infer synapse properties
buildSteps.detail: The wiring diagram shows where synapses are, but not their strength, receptor type or short-term dynamics. These would have to be estimated from cell type, synapse size and molecular labels — a major source of error.

buildSteps.title: Choose model fidelity
buildSteps.detail: Each neuron is replaced by a mathematical model, from a simple point neuron up to a multi-compartment model with dendrites and ion channels. Higher fidelity needs far more compute but captures more of the brain's behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Simulate the network
buildSteps.detail: The model runs on a large computer or neuromorphic chip. Estimates for emulating a human brain in real time range from many petaflops to exaflops, and even the largest current machines have not run a whole mammalian brain at full detail in real time.

buildSteps.title: Connect input and output
buildSteps.detail: The emulation needs sensory streams and a way to act, either in a virtual body or through hardware. This is the point at which it would begin to behave like a person rather than a recording.

buildSteps.title: Validate against the original
buildSteps.detail: Activity and behaviour are compared with data from the living person or animal. Without a validated test for consciousness, this remains a proxy — matching behaviour, not proving inner experience.

buildSteps.title: Run and maintain it
buildSteps.detail: The emulation would need continuous power, redundant storage and backups against hardware failure. Whether a pause, copy or restart preserves identity is unresolved and is a philosophical question, not an engineering one.

prerequisites.tech: Synapse-resolution connectomics of a whole human brain
prerequisites.why: complete connectomes exist only for small organisms — the nematode C. elegans and, in 2024, the adult fruit fly — not for any mammal, let alone a human.

prerequisites.tech: Readout of synaptic strength and dynamics
prerequisites.why: electron microscopy reveals structure, not the weights and time constants a simulation needs; these can only be inferred indirectly today.
the largest supercomputers can simulate fractions of a mammalian brain, not a whole human one, and not faster than biology.

prerequisites.tech: Preservation of an intact human brain
prerequisites.why: chemical fixation and cryo-preservation preserve structure imperfectly, and perfusion quality varies across a whole human brain.
no accepted method exists to confirm that an emulation is conscious, so the central claim of the technology cannot currently be verified.

pathway.milestone: connectomes of small brains and mammalian cortical chunks
pathway.unlocks: proof that automated reconstruction can scale, and benchmarks for segmentation and synapse detection.

pathway.milestone: a complete mouse brain connectome and functional simulation of its cortical circuits
pathway.unlocks: the first full wiring diagram of a mammal and methods for linking structure to behaviour.

pathway.milestone: emulation of significant human cortical circuits on large computers
pathway.unlocks: useful neuroscience and, perhaps, brain-inspired computing — but not a person.

pathway.milestone: hypothetical whole human emulation with sensory embodiment
pathway.unlocks: whatever it is that such a system would be — the ethical, legal and identity questions would arrive before the technology does.
